source.purpose: Verify completeness of GitHub REST list-based scans used for repository workflow/PR/issue inventory and plan decision evidence
source.cost_quota: free official documentation; no authenticated API usage or paid credit required
source.reliability_limits: Documentation explains general pagination; individual endpoints have their own pagination support and page-size defaults. A GitHub connector returning first page only cannot prove complete inventory.

learning.title: GitHub REST inventory completeness requires following next-page links
learning.claim: GitHub REST API list endpoints can return only the first page (often 30 records; most endpoints cap per_page at 100); a successful HTTP 200 is not proof of an exhaustive inventory, and the Link rel=next header identifies additional pages.
learning.decision: GITHUB_REST_PAGINATION_COMPLETENESS_GATE: for list-based PR/issue/workflow/commit inventories, follow Link rel=next until exhausted or explicitly mark result PARTIAL with last cursor, pages scanned, and observed count; never assert all-green or full inventory from a connector known to return only page one. This does not apply to direct complete JSON source_catalog/learning_ledger file reads. Use fail-closed consumer test with >100 synthetic records and verify all IDs and no silent truncation.
learning.next_measurement: Grok: implement a negative test showing first-page-only scans fail completeness; positive test follows rel=next across at least 2 pages; record commit SHA, test run ID, total count and applied_learning_ids in system consumer report. No changes to PayoutLens.
failure_history: Prior automation run 2026-10-10 10:27 discovered pagination risk but could not persist promotion; no verified complete repository inventory is claimed.
fallback_history: If the connector does not expose Link headers or a next-page cursor, label result PARTIAL/bridge_failure and avoid full-inventory claims; use a pagination-capable API client only with verified access.
